HOL foundations for authoring

These summarize the approved system. Bruce resolves discrepancies; current cards and rules are the source, not earlier editions.

Resolution

Roll only for uncertainty with consequences. Correct fictional action may reveal a clue without a roll. The DA asks for Brawn, Fortitude, Agility, Guile, Knowledge or Reason; the player takes an action which may call for that roll. Force is an action, not another attribute or a separate skill-roll category.

Roll 3d6 plus one attribute. Weak is 8 or below: progress, not automatic success. Standard is 9–14. Strong is 15 or above. Three natural retained sixes give Strong plus a benefit; three retained ones give Weak plus a complication.

Boons and Banes cancel. Use at most three net extra dice, retaining the best or worst three. Difficulty comes through Banes, never another target number on the same roll. A cumulative task’s progress target is a different thing: 1/2/3 progress per Weak/Standard/Strong result.

Turns and attacks

At combat start, one unmodified 3d6: 12+ gives players the first turn, otherwise the opposing side starts. Alternate sides; each side chooses its next character. The same side starts every round. Each character has Main, Maneuver, Reaction and movement. Main converts to Maneuver, Maneuver to movement; never upward.

Player attacks use one attacker roll, even against a player. NPC attacks use the player’s defense roll. Strong defense receives Weak attack effects, Standard receives Standard, Weak receives Strong. The defense itself spends no Reaction. Players roll their controlled creatures’ printed attack and defense attributes. For NPC-only actions, either a player or the DA assuming the player role rolls. For an NPC-versus-NPC attack, roll the defender’s printed defense attribute and read the attacker’s defense-outcome table. For consequential NPC healing or other tasks, roll the acting NPC’s printed attribute and outcomes. Apply the ordinary modifiers and use one roll; handling the dice does not transfer control of the NPC. Off-screen events may be resolved by DA judgment without simulating combat.

Damage is fixed by the card. Apply the highest resistance of each matching type, cap 3; do not sum matching armor. Minimum 1 damage applies to the whole damaging event, not each component. Physical is one type. Different resistances coexist. Conditions and displacement may matter more than a larger damage number.

Numerical weakness — approved October 16, 2026: Weakness X increases the matching damage component by X before resistance. Apply each weakness once per damaging event. Use the highest applicable weakness of each type, not the sum of multiple sources, with a normal cap of 3. A damaging effect must include that type; weakness does not add an absent damage type.

Example: Fire Weakness 2 changes 3 fire damage to 5 before resistance. An event dealing 4 physical and 1 fire instead becomes 4 physical and 3 fire; an event dealing only 4 physical is unchanged. Apply matching resistances next.

Special vulnerabilities, such as fire stopping regeneration, use their printed procedure. They do not imply numerical weakness or extra damage unless stated.

Movement

Normal squares cost 1, difficult 2. Diagonal movement costs 1. Standing costs 2 movement. Cannot cross an occupied square unless its occupant is prone; then cost 2 and never end there. Forced movement consumes the entered terrain’s cost; any positive remaining budget can enter the final square and stop even if that cost exceeds the budget.

Forced collisions gather movable occupants into one moving group. All take the collision damage using movement remaining at contact, before deducting the newly struck creature’s Stability. If movement remains, the group continues together. A hard obstruction stops the group and adds 1 to remaining-budget collision damage. The original mover bounces one square opposite afterward if possible.

Group placement — approved October 16, 2026: move the group along the forced movement path and finish in separate legal spaces. If everyone cannot fit, stop at the last position where they can. The DA determines the exact arrangement; placement cannot pass through walls or grant extra forward movement. The original mover’s backward bounce still applies where possible.

All actors have @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.5ebfaad0d5ed6813.JournalEntryPage.3292b6a49dcf7236]{Stability}: default 0, explicit grants only, maximum 3, highest source. It consumes forced movement once per newly struck creature, including through a collision chain; no protection against Prone or conditions.

Conditions

Resolve a temporary numbered condition at turn end, then reduce by 1. Burning and Freezing deal their rating in matching elemental damage; Bleeding bypasses resistance. Poisoned applies its rating in Banes, not damage. Frightened supplies Banes while the stated source is perceptible. Slowed reduces Speed.

Dazed 1/2/3 leaves two/one/no categories among Main, Maneuver and Reaction; choose at turn start. Movement remains. Paralyzed stops actions and movement at any positive rating; its number is duration. Blinded and Deafened numbers are duration, not severity. An asterisk prevents automatic decay; a persistent binary sense loss needs only rating 1*. Removal follows the source.

Grappled prevents movement and reduces action choices like Dazed; it is maintained, not decaying. The grappler suffers their own contribution too. Force can reduce Grappled while Main is retained; rating 3 needs help. Attacks gain Boons equal to the actual target’s Grappled rating. Greater restriction applies when combined with Dazed, not their sum. Prone is binary. Hidden is universal, not observer-by-observer.

A mixed permanent/temporary bookkeeping rule is recorded in the full condition reference. Do not let a new temporary effect become permanent merely because another is starred.

Summons, exploration and recovery

Summoned forms — approved October 16, 2026: summons are shaped from energies to resemble and act like their creatures, not actual physical creatures brought into the scene. They cannot be healed and disappear at 0 HP, leaving no body. Ordinary unsummoned creatures retain their own healing rules.

Summoned forms remain tangible: they occupy squares, block movement, take damage and can be pushed or grappled normally unless their card says otherwise. Their energy composition grants no automatic incorporeality or damage/control immunity.

Summons require commands; see the @UUID[Compendium.heroes-of-legend.player-rules.JournalEntry.56367e2f9016dd21.JournalEntryPage.9ff12960a5e160cc]{summoning reference}. Without a command they do nothing, including following, lookout and alerts. Old orders grant no continued activity; existing conditions and durations still resolve. No free independent turns, inherent Reactions or summon chains. No count cap. Beyond 6 squares from the controller they disappear, including forced movement of either participant. Measure between the nearest occupied squares of controller and summon, using ordinary grid distance; this applies to every footprint. Exactly 6 squares is within the tether; beyond 6 causes immediate disappearance.

Summoned healing — approved October 16, 2026: the controller pays the healing ability’s printed HP cost instead of the summon, once, before resolution. Payment bypasses resistance and must leave the controller above 0 HP. Use the summon’s printed attribute and outcomes. Ordinary unsummoned healers pay their own cost.

Ordinary travel has no routine roll and no exhaustion track. Group checks occur outside combat only: each participant adds 1/2/3 to a declared target. State binary or cumulative before rolling. No group crafting, recipe derivation or wound treatment.

After a safe breath, restore full HP. Grit expenditure and wounds persist. Player characters enter Dying at 0; creatures normally die there. Attacks are lethal unless an explicit ability permits a different outcome; grapple/restraint can capture.
